It replaces traditional scalar fields to reduce storage and preserve sharp features, supporting any cell-based triangulation method [S1, S2].

The claim consists of three parts: 1) 'replaces traditional scalar fields to reduce storage and preserve sharp features', 2) 'supports any cell-based triangulation method', and 3) 'supporting any cell-based triangulation method [S1, S2]'. Source [S2] explicitly supports the first part, stating they choose a mixed form representation 'instead of a traditional used scalar field' and noting that the ray structure reduces samples significantly (reducing storage/computation) while using Hermite data (position and normal) to represent volume data 'as precise as possible' (preserving sharp features). However, Source [S1] notes that the format 'supports any cell-based triangulation method', but Source [S2] does not make this specific claim; instead, it mentions using the representation for 'cubical marching squares algorithm' and 'fast CSG operations'. Therefore, the claim that *both* sources support the triangulation method aspect is incorrect, as only S1 does. Thus, the verdict is partial.
